episode_title: From Meta Recruiter to Full-Time Career Coach: What It Really Takes
question: What advice does Marina Petrovich give to people considering leaving corporate to start a career coaching business?
transcript_excerpt: Marina advises not to quit your job until you have a clear plan, but set a firm deadline for yourself. She spent a year preparing by building her LinkedIn following to 40K, taking business courses to understand systems and processes, and testing the concept before her Meta contract ended in December. She emphasizes: do not quit until you have that figured out, but have a deadline because without it you will keep pushing it. She also recommends getting your first three clients before quitting, as one client is luck, two is a trend, three is a process.

episode_title: From Meta Recruiter to Full-Time Career Coach: What It Really Takes
question: Why is career coaching adoption still so low compared to real estate agents and financial advisors?
transcript_excerpt: Career coaching adoption is only 2 to 10 percent while real estate agents are used by 90+ percent and financial advisors by 20 to 40 percent, despite career choices being equally impactful on retirement and housing decisions. The barrier is the payment model: real estate agents and financial advisors are paid on the backend (commission or assets under management), so clients do not write a check upfront. Until career coaches can normalize backend payment models similar to financial advisors, the industry will struggle to grow adoption.

episode_title: From Meta Recruiter to Full-Time Career Coach: What It Really Takes
question: How did Marina Petrovich build her LinkedIn following to 40K before launching Decode full-time?
transcript_excerpt: Marina built her LinkedIn followers to 40K in one year while still employed at Meta, before she started going into coaching full-time. She did this as part of her deliberate preparation strategy during her year of maternity employment from January to December, testing the market and building her personal brand before officially launching her business.

episode_title: From Meta Recruiter to Full-Time Career Coach: What It Really Takes
question: What is the key difference between transactional recruiting at Meta or Google versus relationship-based career coaching?
transcript_excerpt: In recruiting roles at Meta and Google, the relationship feels transactional because you deal with high volume, your incentive is to represent the company, and if a candidate does not make it you move on to the next with a generic email. In career coaching, the client is the job seeker and your incentive is to make sure they are happy and get the job, so the company becomes the transaction—if it does not work out with one employer, you move to the next together.

episode_title: From Meta Recruiter to Full-Time Career Coach: What It Really Takes
question: What was Marina Petrovich's biggest regret in her first year as a full-time entrepreneur running Decode?
transcript_excerpt: Marina's biggest regret was not testing the business model by taking on actual clients before leaving her corporate job. She knew the business would work because of her background, but in retrospect she wishes she had validated this assumption by working with real clients during her preparation year, rather than relying solely on her confidence and recruiter experience.
